clue.text: Take off in an aeroplane

parts.note: a plane's take-off is literally a start made by flying, which is also the idiom for getting off to a quick, advantageous beginning

explanation.surface: A simple description of a plane leaving the runway.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an excellent beginning with early advantage, and a plane's take-off is literally a beginning in flight.

clue.text: Fifty-one alter version that is word for word

parts.note: LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals

indicators.note: a new version of the word alter is a rearranged form of its letters

explanation.surface: A translator's attempt at an exact rendering of some text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' is the anagram signal; 'alter' looks like a verb but is the fodder, and LI is the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal translation follows the original exactly, without paraphrase.

clue.text: Encouragement at home I have to include small amount of money

indicators.note: the pair of pieces takes another piece within them

parts.note: being in means being at home
contracted to I've
a cent is a coin of little value

explanation.surface: Someone at home offers a little cash as encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' is the container signal: the cash sits between the home word and the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: An incentive is a motivating spur or inducement to act.

clue.text: Look through the space at the dance

indicators.note: the word for look passes through the middle of the word for space

parts.note: a gap is a space or opening
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Peering through an opening at a dance taking place.
explanation.definitionFit: A galop is a lively nineteenth-century ballroom dance in quick time.

clue.text: It's a big blow in the China seas and West Pacific

definitions.text: It's a big blow in the China seas and West Pacific

parts.words: It's a big blow in the China seas and West Pacific
parts.note: a big blow is a violent wind, and the regional name for a tropical cyclone in those waters is wanted

explanation.surface: A weather report about strong winds in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name given to a tropical cyclone in the western Pacific, a violent storm wind.

clue.text: Retains newly-made wine from Greece

indicators.note: remaking the word retains forms its letters in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A Greek vintage keeps its character when freshly made.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white or rosé wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: More demanding Dickensian

parts.note: reads as a fussy character from Dickens, but points to the workhouse boy who famously asked for more gruel

explanation.surface: A character from Dickens who is especially exacting.
explanation.definitionFit: The orphan hero of the Dickens novel famously holds up his bowl and asks for more food.

clue.text: One side of Dundee

definitions.meaning: Dundee ... is a Scottish football team, a side from that city

explanation.surface: Identifying one part of the Scottish city of Dundee.
explanation.walkthrough: Dundee United is a Scottish football club; 'side' means team, not a geographic part of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: To be made one is to be joined together, and the football club's name includes this word.

clue.text: Madman put money before lady with twitch

indicators.note: the money piece is placed ahead of the rest

parts.note: L stands for pound, money
Una is a lady's name, the heroine in Spenser's Faerie Queene
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A madman spending money ahead of a lady with a nervous spasm.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the Latin libra, the pound symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdated term for an insane or crazed person.

clue.text: Swift island, one set in Los Angeles

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: a means one
to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: A quick island trip, with one placed in the Californian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Swift is the author Jonathan Swift, not a word for fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The flying island in Gulliver's Travels, written by Jonathan Swift.

clue.text: Tame servant satisfied consumer demand

parts.note: a domestic is a household servant
a consumer of food meeting their own hunger simply ate

explanation.surface: A tame servant met the demand of shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumer demand' sounds economic but means appetite; satisfying it is eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a wild animal under human control, making it docile.

clue.text: Chopping up tree in front of old soldier

indicators.note: the scrambled piece sits inside the word for front

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard

indicators.note: cutting the word tree into pieces reshuffles its letters

explanation.surface: Someone cutting down a tree in front of an elderly ex-serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopping up' makes ETER from TREE, which goes 'in' VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone with long service, especially a former member of the armed forces.

clue.text: Condition of one sectarian initially in the clutches of terrorist

indicators.note: held inside, gripped by the outer word

parts.note: Provo is slang for a member of the Provisional IRA
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: only the opening letter of sectarian is used

explanation.surface: A hostage condition: one sectarian held by a terrorist.
explanation.walkthrough: Provo is informal British usage for a Provisional IRA member.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a stipulation or qualifying clause in an agreement.

clue.text: Red-headed lady going round the lake

parts.note: the head of the word red is its first letter, R

indicators.note: the word lady is turned round so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: A red-haired woman walks around the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' is the reversal signal. Rydal Water is a small lake in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Rydal Water is a small lake in Cumbria's Lake District, near Wordsworth's home.

clue.text: Imply, in wrongdoing, you, say, took food

parts.note: a sin is wrongdoing

indicators.note: signals a letter that is pronounced like the word you

parts.note: the word you, pronounced
ate means took food

explanation.surface: Suggesting, in a wrongdoing accusation, that you ate something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' shows the letter U is pronounced the same as 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to hint at something unpleasant indirectly rather than state it.

clue.text: It's found on a car coming from food shop in a sense!

indicators.note: the shop's name goes inside the word for a sense

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses
a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

explanation.surface: Something on a car traced to a food shop, sensibly.
explanation.definitionFit: A small parking lamp at the front or side of a vehicle.

clue.text: He wanted a change when he took the lead

indicators.note: changing the order of the letters of the phrase rearranges them

explanation.surface: A man wanted a change when he got ahead of the others.
explanation.definitionFit: To go in front of the others is to take the lead; the phrase also means proceeded.

clue.text: Uncharged particle coming from nerve-cell, about time

indicators.note: the nerve-cell word wraps around the time letter

parts.note: a neuron is a nerve cell

explanation.surface: A neutral particle emerging from a nerve-cell around a certain time.
explanation.definitionFit: A subatomic particle with no electric charge found in atomic nuclei.

clue.text: Found the total pointed to a reasonable conclusion

explanation.surface: Doing a sum and finding that everything made sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both summed figures and, idiomatically, made logical sense.

clue.text: Commander in inspection area found ornamental loop

indicators.note: the commander's letters go inside the pit

parts.note: a pit is the sunken area in a garage for inspecting cars from below
CO is commanding officer

explanation.surface: A commanding officer spotting decorative loops during an inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a small decorative loop on the edge of lace or ribbon.

clue.text: Painter produced small picture as well

parts.note: pic is short for picture
so, as in 'well, so...', a filler word

explanation.surface: An artist painted a small image too.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the famous Spanish painter and co-founder of Cubism.

clue.text: Flighty creature found within a second or two

indicators.note: the bird's name sits inside the words of the phrase

explanation.surface: Something quick discovered in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found within' points to the letters running across 'second or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A condor is a huge vulture, a bird, so a creature of flight.

clue.text: Like this below, it's healthier

parts.note: so means in this way, like this
under means below

explanation.surface: A remark that something lower down is better for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound means in good health, so the comparative means in better health.

clue.text: It is made to measure

parts.note: made-to-measure suggests tailoring, but this is an object made for the purpose of measuring lengths

explanation.surface: Describing a tailored item.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight-edged strip marked with units, used for measuring lengths.

clue.text: Not saying very much about non-clerical study inside

indicators.note: the study word goes inside the non-clerical word

parts.note: laic means lay, not of the clergy
to con is to study

explanation.surface: A taciturn person on a secular course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic means terse, using few words, from the brevity of Spartan speech.

clue.text: Said to be the path of a lady on the day of the union

definitions.text: of a lady on the day of the union

indicators.note: signals a word that is pronounced just like another

parts.note: a bridle path is a track for horse riders

explanation.surface: Describing the route a woman takes on her wedding day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said to be' points to the sound of 'bridle', as in bridle path.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a bride or a wedding, the union of a couple.

clue.text: Turn at cricket, say, in Hampshire town

parts.note: a go is a turn
cricket is an example of a sport

explanation.surface: Someone takes a turn batting in a town in Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county on England's south coast; Gosport is a naval town opposite Portsmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gosport is a town on Portsmouth Harbour in Hampshire.

clue.text: A great idea that's breathtaking?

definitions.meaning: the taking in of breath, inhalation

explanation.surface: A brilliant idea described as astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breathtaking' looks like praise but literally means drawing in a breath.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a flash of genius and the physiological act of inhaling.
